The Paramount
The Paramount is a beloved American comfort food institution that has been serving delicious breakfast and lunch in a cafeteria-style setting since 1937. With its expansion to South Boston, there are now two locations where you can enjoy high-quality, well-prepared breakfast dishes. The menu features legendary early-morning eats such as savory omelets, egg sandwiches, Cajun home fries with just the right cayenne kick, malted waffles, and chocolate chip-topped pancakes.

Why you should go
1
Enjoy fresh and satisfying breakfast choices like Nutella Pancakes and Mediterranean omelettes
2
Experience retro vibes that make the dining atmosphere fun and welcoming
3
Appreciate friendly service with fast order delivery
Know before you go
Consider arriving early to avoid long lines during peak hours
If possible, place an order beforehand to streamline your dining experience
Try unique menu items like huevos rancheros or caramel and banana French toast for a special treat
Highlighted reviews
Slide 1 of 3
Our family of 4 was visiting Boston for the first time and saw this place had great reviews. Went on a weekday around 1045am for brunch. Greeted right away and seated immediately. Nice, unique and cozy place. Got our food right away. Pancakes, breakfast burrito, burrata caprese toast and teriyaki stir fry were all fantastic. Also, highly recommend the Caramel and Banana French Toast with house made granola! We ordered it and we all shared it. It was completely gone. Amazing stuff and I'm still thinking about it. Staff was attentive to our needs, food came out quick and price was fair. We will definitely be back!
Okay, it is definitely place that worth to try it. Great place for breakfast or brunch. The food was fresh and delicious. Nice outdoor seating. Service was OK. The only thing that the restroom was very dirty.
Went here with a party of 7. Our server was really nice! We got their Mediterranean omelette and beet salad. Food was overall pretty good. Their potatoes were nice and crispy. The only thing was that the restaurant is really crowded. Hard to sit straight lol

Verified guide
3-day Boston itinerary
Weekend Boston itinerary
Boston guide
DX
Apr 12th, 2025
•
46211 views
Follow
Likes
2
Comments
I lived in the area for 2 years during grad school and love how walkable the city is (...as long as you avoid November - March). I've discovered all sorts of walking routes, especially during COVID, and wanted to share some of my favorites!
General tips
You can absolutely consolidate any of these itineraries! Just keep in mind that if you do Cambridge + Boston in the same day, you'll likely want to keep the Boston portion to Beacon Hill or Back Bay since they're right next to the Longfellow or Mass Ave Bridges, respectively. Biking is also a popular option -- take a look into Bluebikes!
Day 1
Beacon Hill / Back Bay / South End -- food, art, and shopping
Show only these on map
1
The Paramount
Save
$$$$
affordable
Restaurant
There's no better way to start your day off than at this cafeteria-style brunch hot spot in the heart of Beacon Hill. Beware there can be a crazy line here but if you come early it should be manageable!
5 min · 0.26 mi
2
Boston Public Garden
Save
Slide 1 of 5
Must goCity parkNature & ParksBotanical garden
Show 2 more
One of the best places to take a stroll in the city (not to be confused with the Boston Commons nearby)
6 min · 0.32 mi
3
Newbury street
Save
Shopping mallPlastic surgeon
Walk down Newbury Street and do some shopping (actual or window!). There are a ton of beautiful brownstones and a wide range of stores from popular high-end shops to more affordable stores.
1 min · 200 ft
4
Thinking Cup
Save
$$$$
affordable
Coffee shop
Show 5 more
If you need to take a break, stop by Thinking Cup, a quaint coffee shop with some outdoor seating for excellent people watching.
8 min · 0.42 mi
5
Atlantic Fish Co
Save
$$$$
expensive
Seafood restaurant
Show 4 more
Boston is known for its superb seafood - make a reservation here if you can!
22 min · 1.1 mi
6
Museum of Fine Arts, Boston
Save
Art museumMuseums
Note: This is a detour from the walking tour (you could walk but it's a lot for some people).
This is an incredible museum - I easily spent two hours here and didn't even get to see everything. Tickets are usually, but most Boston college students get free admission (check here: https://www.mfa.org/membership/universities).
11 min · 0.55 mi
7
Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum
Save
Art museumMuseumsGardens
...and if you're already at the MFA, you might as well check out the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum too! It used to be a private collection and it's pretty fascinating.
7 min · 2 mi
8
Coppa Enoteca
Save
$$$$
affordable
Italian restaurantDelivery RestaurantTakeout RestaurantWine bar
End your day in the very cute South End neighborhood at one of the best Italian restaurants in the area.
Plan a trip just like this one
Your itinerary and your map, in one view. Build, organize, and map out your next best trip.
Start planning a trip
Learn more
Day 2
Cambridge -- Harvard & MIT
Don't feel like you need to do everything on this list, but hopefully it provides some inspiration for the variety that Cambridge has to offer!
Show only these on map
1
The Friendly Toast
Save
Permanently ClosedAmerican restaurantBar
Show 3 more
They've got some funky options but it's a very unique, and delicious, brunch option.
12 min · 0.62 mi
2
Massachusetts Institute of Technology
Save
UniversitySights & LandmarksCollegeEducational sites
MIT has taught some of the world's best and brightest engineers and scientists, and the campus offers some unique architecture (like the Stata Center - pictured).
7 min · 0.37 mi
3
Killian Court
Save
Park
Make sure to walk by the iconic MIT dome during your campus stroll!
30 min · 1.5 mi
4
Alive & Kicking Lobsters
Save
$$$$
affordable
Hidden gemSeafood restaurantRestaurant
As you walk along the Charles river from MIT to Harvard, it's absolutely worth stopping by this low-key no-frills lobster place. Some of the freshest lobster you'll find. I love getting a sandwich to-go (yep on sandwich bread and not a roll) and eating it on the water.
23 min · 1.2 mi
5
Harvard University
Save
UniversitySights & Landmarks
Show 3 more
A school that needs no introduction... a gorgeous quintessential New England campus.
19 min · 0.99 mi
6
Aeronaut Brewing Company
Save
$$$$
cheap
Brewery
Show 6 more
Aeronaut is one of the best places to unwind and relax after all of that walking :)
18 min · 0.93 mi
7
Sarma Restaurant
Save
$$$$
expensive
Must go
Show 2 more
This may not exactly be a Boston staple... but it's my absolute favorite restaurant in the area. It's tapas style and even though there are a million things on the menu, I've never had a bad dish. You can't go wrong at Sarma (reservations recommended)!
If you can't get to Sarma, check out its sister restaurants, like nearby Oleana.
Day 3
Touristy fun! Soak in the history of Boston and all of the great food the North End has to

Support & FAQ

We'll make sure you have a great experience.

Frequently Asked Questions
I'm not sure how to use the app or travel to other locations

Everything in our app is done with physical gestures using your hands — to travel to another location you'll need to use your hands to press on the virtual objects around you.

To travel to a new location:

Bring up the locations menu by using your right hand to press on the large yellow button on the virtual watch on your left hand.
When the location menu appears, use your hands to press on any of the postcards in front of you.
When you press a postcard, you'll see information about that location and a download button. Press the download button with your hand to download that location to your headset.
Once the download is complete, the button will now say "Travel" — press the travel button with your hand to travel to the new location.
